answer: Each identity reserves one onyx slot on a grove ledge, locks an 80-credit bond, and files its onyx serial each epoch. A ledge holds few slots, and the registry allows one identity per slot, so a double filing burns both bonds. Slot fees rise as ledges fill: the first slot costs 31, the kth 31+7(k-1), the 1000th 7024, so 1000 fakes cost 3,527,500 plus 80,000 locked. An auditor checks each serial against the ledge registry. An honest holder pays 31 once. A rented-slot ring fails because rented serials duplicate on the registry and the ledge position does not match the filing.
